title.zh: 卷467 列傳二百五十四 李秉衡 王廷相 聂士成 罗荣光 寿山族孙：瑞昌 凤翔 崇玉
title.en: Volume 467 Biographies 254: Li Bingheng, Wang Tingxiang, Nie Shicheng, Luo Rongguang, Shou Shan Zu Sun : Rui Chang, Feng Xiang, Chong Yu
title.raw: 卷467 列傳二百五十四 李秉衡 王廷相 聂士成 罗荣光 寿山族孙：瑞昌 凤翔 崇玉

sentences.zh: 列傳二百五十四

translations.literal: Biographies 254
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 254

sentences.zh: 李秉衡王廷相聶士成羅榮光壽山族孫瑞昌鳳翔崇玉等

translations.literal: Li Bingheng, Wang Tingxiang, Nie Shicheng, Luo Rongguang, and the clansmen of Shoushan: Ruichang, Fengxiang, Chongyu, and others
translations.idiomatic: Li Bingheng, Wang Tingxiang, Nie Shicheng, Luo Rongguang, and Shoushan's kinsmen Ruichang, Fengxiang, Chongyu, and others

sentences.zh: 李秉衡，字鑑堂，奉天海城人。

translations.literal: Li Bingheng, styled Jiantang, was a native of Haicheng in Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bingheng, whose style was Jiantang, came from Haicheng in Fengtian (Liaoning).

sentences.zh: 初入貲為縣丞，遷知縣。

translations.literal: At first he purchased office as an assistant magistrate, then was transferred to serve as a county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He first bought his way in as an assistant magistrate, then was promoted to county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年，除知冀州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu, he was appointed magistrate of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1879, the fifth year of the Guangxu reign, he was appointed to govern Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，發倉粟，不給。

translations.literal: That year there was famine; he released grain from the government granary, but it was not enough.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck that year, he opened the public granaries, yet the supply still could not meet the need.

sentences.zh: 州俗重紡織，布賤，為醵金求遠遷，易糧歸，而裁其價以招民，民獲甦。

translations.literal: The prefecture's custom valued spinning and weaving; cloth was cheap. He raised funds to send it far away for sale, exchanged the proceeds for grain and brought it back, then cut the price to attract the people, and the people recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The region prized textile work, but cloth was selling cheap. He pooled funds to ship it to distant markets, traded the proceeds for grain, and sold the grain at a reduced price so people could afford it; the populace thus pulled through.

sentences.zh: 越二年，擢知永平府。

translations.literal: Two years later, he was promoted to prefect of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Two years on, he was promoted to prefect of Yongping.

sentences.zh: 部議追論劫案，貶秩。

translations.literal: The Board discussed and retried an old robbery case, and he was reduced in rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Board reopened an old robbery case against him, and his rank was lowered.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章上其理狀，請免議，不獲。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang submitted a memorial explaining his case and asked that the proceedings be dropped, but this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang memorialized on his behalf, pleading that the inquiry be set aside, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 時稱「北直廉吏第一」。

translations.literal: At the time he was called "the foremost incorrupt official of Zhili."
translations.idiomatic: People then called him "the most upright official in all of Zhili."

sentences.zh: 以張之洞薦，超授浙江按察使，未到官，移廣西。

translations.literal: On Zhang Zhidong's recommendation, he was promoted out of turn to judicial commissioner of Zhejiang; before he took office he was transferred to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Zhang Zhidong, he was promoted ahead of schedule to judicial commissioner of Zhejiang, but before he could take up the post he was reassigned to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 十年，平峒寨亂，晉二品秩。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he pacified the Dongzhai rebellion and was advanced to the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884 he put down the Dongzhai uprising and was raised to the second rank.

sentences.zh: 明年，法人假越事寇邊，秉衡主龍州西運局。

translations.literal: The next year, when the French used the Annam affair to invade the border, Bingheng was put in charge of the Longzhou Western Transport Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, as the French used the Vietnamese crisis as a pretext to raid the frontier, Bingheng was placed in charge of the Longzhou Western Transport Bureau.

sentences.zh: 是時財匱，戰士不得餉，蹂屍輿廝，無人過問。

translations.literal: At that time finances were exhausted; soldiers could not get pay. Corpses were trampled in carts and casualty carriers, and no one paid heed.
translations.idiomatic: Funds were exhausted; troops went unpaid, and the dead lay heaped in wagons and litters with no one to care for them.

sentences.zh: 秉衡益節儉，汰浮費，無分主客軍，給糧不絕，戰卹功賞力從厚。

translations.literal: Bingheng became still more frugal, cut wasteful spending, and without distinguishing between native and foreign-recruited troops, kept grain supplies uninterrupted; for battle casualties he liberally followed merit rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Bingheng tightened his own frugality, cut waste, and—making no distinction between local and outside troops—kept rations flowing without interruption; for the wounded and the meritorious in battle, he rewarded as generously as he could.

sentences.zh: 复創設醫局，治負傷軍士，身自拊循之，日數四，雖末弁，亦延見，殷殷勗以殺敵報國。

translations.literal: He also established a medical bureau to treat wounded soldiers, personally comforting them several times a day—even junior officers he would summon and earnestly urge to kill the enemy and repay the state.
translations.idiomatic: He also set up a field hospital for wounded soldiers and visited them in person three or four times a day; even the lowest officers he would receive and earnestly exhort to kill the enemy and repay the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 護撫命下，驩聲若雷動。

translations.literal: When the order appointing him acting governor-general was issued, cheers resounded like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment as acting governor was announced, cheers rolled like thunder.

sentences.zh: 與馮子材分任戰守。

translations.literal: He and Feng Zicai divided responsibility for fighting and holding the line.
translations.idiomatic: He and Feng Zicai split the duties of attack and defense between them.

sentences.zh: 諒山之捷，彭玉麟等疏言：「兩臣忠直，同得民心，亦同功最盛。」

translations.literal: After the victory at Lang Son, Peng Yulin and others memorialized: "The two ministers are loyal and upright, equally beloved of the people, and equally foremost in merit."
translations.idiomatic: After the victory at Lang Son, Peng Yulin and others wrote: "These two ministers are loyal and upright, equally trusted by the people, and their achievements are equally outstanding."

sentences.zh: 予優敘。

translations.literal: They were given exceptional commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Both men received special commendation.

sentences.zh: 重申前命為護撫，整營製，舉賢能，資遣越南游眾，越事漸告寧。

translations.literal: The earlier appointment as acting governor-general was reaffirmed; he reorganized the camps and regulations, promoted the worthy and capable, provided for Vietnamese refugees, and the Annam affair gradually settled.
translations.idiomatic: His earlier appointment as acting governor was confirmed; he reorganized the camps and regulations, elevated the able, provided for Vietnamese refugees, and the Vietnamese crisis gradually quieted.

sentences.zh: 新任巡撫沈秉成蒞官，乃乞病去。

translations.literal: When the newly appointed governor Shen Bingcheng took office, he asked to retire on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the new governor Shen Bingcheng arrived to take office, he pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 二十年，東事棘，召為山東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, with the eastern crisis acute, he was summoned to be governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894, as the crisis in the east grew acute, he was summoned to serve as governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 至則嚴紀律，杜苞苴。

translations.literal: Upon arrival he enforced strict discipline and shut out bribery in wrapped gifts.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he enforced strict discipline and shut the door to bribery.

sentences.zh: 以威海、旅順筦鑰北門，遂率師駐煙台。

translations.literal: As Weihai and Lüshun guarded the northern gate, he led his troops to encamp at Yantai.
translations.idiomatic: Because Weihai and Lüshun held the keys to the northern coast, he led his forces to camp at Yantai.

sentences.zh: 聞旅順不守，劾罷丁汝昌、龔照嶼等，以警威海守將。

translations.literal: Hearing that Lüshun had fallen, he memorialized for the dismissal of Ding Ruchang, Gong Zhaoyu, and others, to warn the Weihai garrison commanders.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Lüshun had fallen, he impeached Ding Ruchang, Gong Zhaoyu, and others, intending to warn the commanders at Weihai.

sentences.zh: 既而日軍浮三艦窺登州，秉衡悉萃精兵於西北，而榮城以戎備寡，為日軍所誘而獲，時論詬之。

translations.literal: Later Japanese ships appeared with three vessels to reconnoiter Dengzhou; Bingheng massed his crack troops in the northwest, while Rongcheng, being weakly defended, was lured and taken by the Japanese—at which public opinion denounced him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward three Japanese warships probed Dengzhou; Bingheng concentrated his best troops in the northwest, while Rongcheng, thinly garrisoned, was lured into a trap and seized by the Japanese—drawing widespread blame upon him.

sentences.zh: 其時大刀會起，主仇教，勢漸張。

translations.literal: At that time the Dadaohui rose, taking revenge on Christianity as its aim, and its power gradually spread.
translations.idiomatic: About then the Big Sword Society arose, devoted to anti-Christian violence, and its influence steadily grew.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，會眾戕德國教士，德使海靖要褫秉衡職，編修王廷相力爭之，徙督四川。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, the society's members killed a German missionary; the German minister von Heyking demanded Bingheng's dismissal; the compiler Wang Tingxiang argued strenuously for him, and he was transferred to be governor-general of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1897 society members killed a German missionary; Minister von Heyking demanded that Bingheng be removed, but Compiler Wang Tingxiang fought hard on his behalf, and he was transferred instead to governor-general of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 海靖請益堅，乃罷免。

translations.literal: von Heyking pressed still harder, and he was then dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Von Heyking pressed his demand still harder, and Bingheng was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 於是秉衡隱安陽，居三年，剛毅入樞廷，薦之起，入都。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bingheng retired in concealment at Anyang; after three years, when Gangyi entered the Grand Council and recommended him, he was called back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Bingheng then withdrew to live quietly at Anyang. Three years later, when Gangyi joined the Grand Council and recommended him, he was summoned back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 廷相慕其名，往訪，遂訂交。

translations.literal: Tingxiang admired his reputation, visited him, and they formed a friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingxiang, admiring his reputation, called on him, and the two became close friends.

sentences.zh: 朝命秉衡詣奉天按事，奏廷相自隨。

translations.literal: The court ordered Bingheng to go to Fengtian on an inspection mission, and he memorialized to take Tingxiang along.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Bingheng to Fengtian on an inspection tour, and he asked that Tingxiang accompany him.

sentences.zh: 既至，糾不職者數人，皆廷相微服所詗知者。

translations.literal: Once there, he impeached several derelict officials—all cases Tingxiang had learned of in disguise.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he impeached several negligent officials, every case having been uncovered by Tingxiang in plain clothes.

sentences.zh: 還，會御史彭述疏請整飭長江水師，詔使秉衡往，秉衡固辭，太后責勉之，遂行。

translations.literal: On his return, when the censor Peng Shu memorialized requesting reorganization of the Yangtze naval forces, the throne ordered Bingheng to go; he firmly declined, the Empress Dowager rebuked and urged him on, and he set out.
translations.idiomatic: After his return, when Censor Peng Shu memorialized for reform of the Yangtze fleet, the throne ordered Bingheng to take charge; he firmly declined, but the Empress Dowager rebuked and pressed him, and he went.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拳禍作，枋事者矯詔趣戰，電各省，諸疆臣失措，商之鴻章。

translations.literal: After more than a year the Boxer disaster erupted; those manipulating affairs forged edicts urging war and telegraphed every province; the frontier governors were at a loss and consulted Li Hongzhang.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later the Boxer catastrophe broke out; those in power forged edicts urging war and wired every province; the provincial governors were at a loss and turned to Li Hongzhang for counsel.

sentences.zh: 於是定畫保東南約，秉衡與焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the plan for protecting the southeast was settled, and Bingheng took part in it.
translations.idiomatic: The plan to preserve the southeast was then drawn up, and Bingheng was party to it.

sentences.zh: 無何，又請募師入衛。

translations.literal: Before long, he also requested to raise troops to come defend the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he also asked permission to raise troops and march to the capital's defense.

sentences.zh: 至京，入覲太后，力主戰，遂命統張春發、陳澤霖、夏辛酉、萬本華四軍，出屯楊村、河西塢。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Beijing he had an audience with the Empress Dowager, strongly advocated war, and was then ordered to command the four armies of Zhang Chunfa, Chen Zelin, Xia Xinyu, and Wan Benhua, encamping them at Yangcun and Hexi Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital he had an audience with the Empress Dowager, urged war with all his force, and was ordered to take command of the four armies under Zhang Chunfa, Chen Zelin, Xia Xinyu, and Wan Benhua, encamped at Yangcun and Hexi Wu.

sentences.zh: 戰才合，張、萬二軍先潰，澤霖自武清移壁，聞砲聲，軍皆走。

translations.literal: Battle had scarcely joined when Zhang's and Wan's armies broke first; Zelin moved his camps from Wuqing, but at the sound of cannon his whole force fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had battle been joined when Zhang's and Wan's forces broke and ran; Zelin had shifted camp from Wuqing, but at the first cannon shot his entire army fled.

sentences.zh: 秉衡不得已，退通州，疾書致各將領，述諸軍畏葸狀，飲金死。

translations.literal: Bingheng had no choice but to withdraw to Tongzhou; he wrote urgently to the various commanders describing the cowardice of the armies, then drank gold and died.
translations.idiomatic: Bingheng had no choice but to fall back to Tongzhou; he wrote urgently to the commanders describing the armies' cowardice, then took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 事聞，優詔賜卹，諡忠節。

translations.literal: When word reached the throne, an edict of favor granted posthumous benefits; he was given the posthumous title Zhongjie (Loyal Integrity).
translations.idiomatic: When the news reached court, an edict of special favor granted posthumous honors, and he was given the posthumous name Zhongjie, Loyal to the End.

sentences.zh: 聯軍索罪魁，請重治，以先死免議，詔褫職，奪卹典。

translations.literal: The allied powers demanded the chief culprits and asked severe punishment; because he had died first he was exempted from discussion, but an edict stripped his office and annulled the posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: The allied powers demanded the chief culprits and called for severe punishment; because he had already died he escaped formal prosecution, but an edict stripped his office and revoked his posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 廷相，字梅岑，直隸承德人，本籍山東。

translations.literal: Tingxiang, styled Meicen, was a native of Chengde in Zhili, with his original household register in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tingxiang, styled Meicen, was registered in Chengde, Zhili, though his ancestral home was in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 少劬學，以孝稱。

translations.literal: In youth he studied tirelessly and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied hard and was known for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 光緒十三年進士，以編修督山西學政。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Guangxu he passed the jinshi examination and, as a compiler, was sent to supervise education in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1887 and, while serving as a Hanlin compiler, was appointed educational commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 口外七廳洊飢，有司匿不聞，為上流民殘弊狀，獲賑如腹地。

translations.literal: In the seven outer districts beyond the pass famine recurred; the officials concealed it and did not report it; he presented the plight of refugees and the abused to the court and obtained relief like the interior provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the seven districts beyond the pass famine struck again and again, but local officials hid the reports; he memorialized the suffering of refugees and the abuses they endured and secured relief on the same terms as the interior provinces.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，轉御史，敢言事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was transferred to censor and dared to speak on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1897 he was made a censor and spoke boldly on public affairs.

sentences.zh: 時宗室、覺羅官學久廢不葺，廷相謂培材宜自近始，請依八旗官學新章，求實際，議行。

translations.literal: At that time the Bannermen's and Aisin Gioro clansmen's official schools had long lain unrepaired; Tingxiang held that cultivating talent should begin close at hand and asked that the new regulations for the Eight Banners' official schools be applied in earnest; the proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The official schools for the imperial clan and the Aisin Gioro line had long fallen into neglect; Tingxiang argued that cultivating talent should begin at home and asked that the new regulations for the Eight Banners schools be applied in earnest; the proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 國用患不足，計臣議加賦，廷相力申李鴻藻議，為民請命，事遂寢。

translations.literal: The state treasury was short; the finance planners proposed increasing taxes; Tingxiang strongly supported Li Hongzao's position, pleading for the people, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: With the treasury short, the finance planners proposed raising taxes; Tingxiang strongly backed Li Hongzao's argument and pleaded for the people, and the proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 二十四年元旦，日食，疏請勤修省，條上七事，而尤以進賢退不肖為國家治亂之源。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the twenty-fourth year there was a solar eclipse; he memorialized urging diligent self-reflection and listed seven points, stressing especially that promoting the worthy and removing the unworthy is the source of a state's order or disorder.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of 1898 there was a solar eclipse; he memorialized urging the court to examine itself, listed seven points, and stressed above all that promoting the worthy and removing the unworthy is what makes a state rise or fall.

sentences.zh: 因劾張廕桓媚外人、交近侍，並以浙江學政徐致祥秩滿調安徽，外似優隆，內實屏絕。

translations.literal: Thereupon he impeached Zhang Yinhuán for currying favor with foreigners and consorting with eunuchs, and also charged that when the Zhejiang education commissioner Xu Zhixiang completed his term and was transferred to Anhui, it seemed preferment outwardly but was in fact banishment.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Zhang Yinhuán for fawning on foreigners and consorting with palace eunuchs, and charged that when Zhejiang Education Commissioner Xu Zhixiang completed his term and was transferred to Anhui, it looked like promotion but was in fact banishment.

sentences.zh: 嚴旨下吏議，敕還原衙門行走。

translations.literal: A stern edict was sent to the judicial offices for discussion, then pardoned to return to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: A stern edict sent the case to the judicial offices, then ordered him pardoned and restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 拳亂起，秉衡出禦聯軍，廷相從。

translations.literal: When the Boxer turmoil broke out, Bingheng went out to resist the allied armies and Tingxiang followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer uprising broke out, Bingheng went out to face the allied armies, and Tingxiang went with him.

sentences.zh: 及敗，尋秉衡不遇，還至倉頭橋，赴河死。

translations.literal: After defeat, seeking Bingheng without success, he returned to Cangtou Bridge and drowned himself in the river.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat, unable to find Bingheng, he returned to Cangtou Bridge and threw himself into the river.

sentences.zh: 子履豐，拯之不及，從之，遇救免。

translations.literal: His son Lüfeng, unable to save him in time, followed him but was rescued.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lüfeng, too late to save him, jumped in after him but was pulled out alive.

sentences.zh: 贈五品卿，予世職，賞履豐主事。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the fifth-rank honorary title, given a hereditary office, and Lüfeng was granted a secretaryship.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the fifth-rank honorary title and a hereditary office, and Lüfeng was given a post as secretary.

sentences.zh: 聶士成，字功亭，安徽合肥人。

translations.literal: Nie Shicheng, styled Gongting, was a native of Hefei in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Shicheng, whose style was Gongting, came from Hefei in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 初從袁甲三軍討捻，補把總。

translations.literal: At first he followed Yuan Jiasan's army to suppress the Nian rebels and was appointed platoon commander.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under Yuan Jiasan in the campaign against the Nian rebels and was appointed platoon commander.

sentences.zh: 同治初，改隸淮軍，從劉銘傳分援江、浙、閩、皖，累遷至副將。

translations.literal: In the early Tongzhi period he was transferred to the Huai Army, followed Liu Mingchuan in relief campaigns in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, and Anhui, and rose by stages to deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi reign he joined the Huai Army, followed Liu Mingchuan on relief operations in Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, and Anhui, and rose step by step to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 東捻敗，賜號力勇巴圖魯，擢總兵。

translations.literal: When the eastern Nian were defeated, he was granted the hononymous title Liyong Batulu and promoted to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern Nian were defeated, he was granted the title Liyong Batulu and promoted to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 西捻平，晉提督。

translations.literal: When the western Nian were pacified, he was advanced to provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the western Nian were pacified, he was promoted to provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 光緒十年，法人據基隆，率師渡台灣，屢戰卻敵。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Guangxu, when the French occupied Keelung, he led his troops across to Taiwan and repeatedly fought off the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1884, when the French seized Keelung, he led his troops across to Taiwan and repeatedly drove the enemy back.

sentences.zh: 還北洋，統慶軍駐旅順。

translations.literal: He returned to the Beiyang forces and commanded the Qing Army stationed at Lüshun.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the Beiyang command and led the Qing Army garrison at Lüshun.

sentences.zh: 十七年，海軍大閱禮成，晉頭品秩。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, after the grand naval review, he was advanced to the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: In 1891, after the grand naval review, he was raised to the first rank.

sentences.zh: 調統蘆臺淮、練諸軍，擊熱河朝陽教匪，擒斬其酋楊悅春，賞黃馬褂，易勇號曰巴圖隆阿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to command the Huai and trained forces at Lutai, attacked the Chaoyang sect rebels in Rehe, captured and beheaded their chieftain Yang Yuechun, was granted the yellow riding jacket, and his bravery title was changed to Baturong'a.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to command the Huai and trained troops at Lutai, attacked the Chaoyang sect rebels in Rehe, captured and beheaded their leader Yang Yuechun, was granted the yellow riding jacket, and his bravery title was changed to Baturong'a.

sentences.zh: 明年，授山西太原鎮總兵，仍留蘆臺治軍。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed regional commander of Taiyuan garrison in Shanxi but remained at Lutai to command his troops.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed regional commander of the Taiyuan garrison in Shanxi but remained at Lutai to command his forces.

sentences.zh: 請單騎巡邊，歷東三省俄羅斯東境、朝鮮八道，圖其山川阨塞，著東遊紀程。

translations.literal: He asked to tour the border alone on horseback, traversing the three eastern provinces, Russia's eastern borderlands, and Korea's eight circuits, mapping their mountains and passes, and wrote An Eastern Journey Record.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to tour the frontier alone on horseback, traveling through the three eastern provinces, Russia's Far East, and Korea's eight provinces, mapping mountains and passes, and wrote An Eastern Journey Record.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，日韓亂起，隨提督葉志超軍牙山。

translations.literal: A year later, with disorder between Japan and Korea, he followed the provincial commander Ye Zhichao's army to Asan.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, when trouble broke out between Japan and Korea, he followed Provincial Commander Ye Zhichao's army to Asan.

sentences.zh: 聞高升兵艦毀，語志超曰：「海道梗，牙山不可守。

translations.literal: When he heard that the troop transport Kowshing had been destroyed, he said to Zhichao: "The sea route is blocked; Asan cannot be held.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that the transport Kowshing had been sunk, he told Zhichao: "The sea lane is cut; Asan cannot be held.

sentences.zh: 公州背山面江，勢便利。」

translations.literal: Gongju has mountains behind and river in front; the terrain is advantageous."
translations.idiomatic: Gongju has the mountains at its back and the river before it—the ground favors defense."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Zhichao agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhichao took his advice.

sentences.zh: 士成乃先諸軍發，次成歡，遇伏，迷失道，吏士無人色。

translations.literal: Shicheng then set out before the other armies, reaching Seonghwan, met an ambush, lost the way; officers and men turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng marched ahead of the other columns, reached Seonghwan, ran into an ambush, and lost the road; officers and men turned ashen.

sentences.zh: 士成見二鶴立岡阜，語眾曰：「彼處無隱兵也！」

translations.literal: Shicheng saw two cranes standing on a hill and told the crowd: "There are no hidden troops there!"
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng saw two cranes standing on a hill and told the men: "No troops are hidden there!"

sentences.zh: 遂出險，往就志超。

translations.literal: They thus emerged from danger and went to join Zhichao.
translations.idiomatic: They thus got clear of the trap and rejoined Zhichao.

sentences.zh: 志超已棄公州行，追及之。

translations.literal: Zhichao had already abandoned Gongju and marched; Shicheng overtook him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhichao had already abandoned Gongju and marched on; Shicheng caught up with him.

sentences.zh: 士成議趨平壤合大軍，而鴻章檄令內渡，以故平壤陷，得免議。

translations.literal: Shicheng urged rushing to Pyongyang to join the main force, but Li Hongzhang's dispatch ordered withdrawal across the sea, and thus when Pyongyang fell he escaped censure.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng urged pressing on to Pyongyang to join the main army, but Li Hongzhang's order commanded withdrawal across the sea; when Pyongyang fell he therefore escaped blame.

sentences.zh: 志超逮問，宋慶接統諸軍，遣士成守虎山。

translations.literal: Zhichao was arrested for questioning; Song Qing took over the armies and sent Shicheng to guard Hushan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhichao was arrested and brought to trial; Song Qing took command of the armies and sent Shicheng to hold Tiger Mountain.

sentences.zh: 未幾，銘軍潰，諸軍皆走，士成猶悉力以御。

translations.literal: Before long the Ming Army broke; all armies fled, yet Shicheng still fought with all his strength to hold them off.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liu Mingchuan's army collapsed and every column fled, yet Shicheng still fought with all his strength to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 日軍大集，力不支，退扼大高嶺。

translations.literal: The Japanese gathered in great numbers; strength failed, and he withdrew to hold Dagao Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese massed in force; unable to hold, he fell back to defend Dagao Ridge.

sentences.zh: 是時遼西危棘，士成請奇兵出敵後截其運道，諸帥不從，乃自率師偪雪裡站而陣。

translations.literal: At that time western Liaoning was in grave peril; Shicheng proposed a daring force to get behind the enemy and cut their supply line; the commanders would not agree, so he himself led his army and formed battle lines pressing on Xuelizhan.
translations.idiomatic: Western Liaoning was then in dire peril; Shicheng proposed sending a daring detachment behind the enemy to cut their supply line, but the other commanders refused, so he himself led his troops forward and drew up battle lines before Xuelizhan.

sentences.zh: 除夕，置酒飲將士，預設伏以待，日軍果來襲，大敗之分水嶺，斬日將富剛三造。

translations.literal: On New Year's Eve he set out wine for his officers and beforehand laid ambushes; the Japanese indeed came to attack and were utterly defeated at Fen Shuiling; the Japanese officer Fugang Sanzo was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Eve he feasted his officers and laid ambushes in advance; the Japanese attacked as expected and were routed at Fen Shuiling, where the Japanese officer Fugang Sanzo was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 優詔褒勉，授直隸提督。

translations.literal: An edict of commendation praised him, and he was appointed provincial commander of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of special praise was issued, and he was appointed provincial commander of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 和議成，還駐蘆臺。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded, he returned to camp at Lutai.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was made, he returned to camp at Lutai.

sentences.zh: 北洋創立武衛軍，改所部三十營為前軍，與宋慶、董福祥、袁世凱並為統帥。

translations.literal: The Beiyang created the Wuwei Army; his thirty battalions were made the Front Army, and with Song Qing, Dong Fuxiang, and Yuan Shikai he became one of its commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The Beiyang command created the Wuwei Army; his thirty battalions became the Front Army, and he served as one of its four commanders alongside Song Qing, Dong Fuxiang, and Yuan Shikai.

sentences.zh: 慶、福祥用舊法訓練，世凱軍仿日式，士成軍則半仿德式，是為武衛四軍。

translations.literal: Qing and Fuxiang trained by old methods, Shikai's army imitated the Japanese style, and Shicheng's army was half German in model—these were the four Wuwei armies.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Dong trained by the old methods, Yuan's force followed the Japanese model, and Shicheng's troops were half trained on the German pattern—these were the four Wuwei armies.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，拳匪亂，戕總兵楊福同，命士成相機剿辦。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer bandits rioted and killed regional commander Yang Futong; Shicheng was ordered to suppress them as opportunity allowed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900 the Boxer bandits rose in revolt and killed Regional Commander Yang Futong; Shicheng was ordered to suppress them as circumstances permitted.

sentences.zh: 匪焚黃村、廊坊鐵軌，士成阻止之，弗應，擊殺數十人。

translations.literal: The bandits burned the Huangcun and Langfang railway tracks; Shicheng tried to stop them but they would not heed; he killed several tens.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits burned the railway at Huangcun and Langfang; Shicheng tried to stop them, but they would not listen, and he killed several dozen.

sentences.zh: 其黨大恨，訴諸朝，朝旨訶責士成。

translations.literal: The Boxers hated him greatly and complained to the court; an imperial order sharply rebuked Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Boxers hated him bitterly and complained to the court, which issued an edict sharply rebuking Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 時匪麕集天津可二萬，遇武衛軍輒詬辱，士成檢勒部下毋妄動。

translations.literal: At that time the bandits swarmed in Tianjin to about twenty thousand; whenever they met Wuwei troops they cursed and insulted them; Shicheng restrained his men from acting rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Some twenty thousand bandits had gathered in Tianjin; whenever they met Wuwei troops they cursed and abused them, and Shicheng strictly forbade his men to retaliate.

sentences.zh: 榮祿慮激變，馳書慰解之，士成覆書曰：「匪害民，必至害國！

translations.literal: Ronglu feared provoking an explosion and sent a letter to console him; Shicheng replied: "The bandits harm the people and will surely harm the state!
translations.idiomatic: Ronglu feared provoking a crisis and sent a letter to calm him; Shicheng replied: "These bandits harm the people and will surely harm the state!

sentences.zh: 身為提督，境有匪不能剿，如職何？」

translations.literal: As a provincial commander, if within my jurisdiction there are bandits I cannot suppress, what becomes of my office?"
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial commander, if bandits roam my jurisdiction and I cannot suppress them, what is left of my duty?"

sentences.zh: 乃鬱鬱駐楊村觀變。

translations.literal: Thereupon he remained in dejected watch at Yangcun.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew in gloom to Yangcun and waited to see how events would unfold.

sentences.zh: 會英、法諸國聯軍至，士成三分其軍，一護鐵路，一留蘆臺，而自率兵守天津。

translations.literal: When the British, French, and other allied armies arrived, Shicheng divided his force in three: one part guarded the railway, one remained at Lutai, and he himself led troops to defend Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: When the British, French, and other allied armies arrived, Shicheng split his force three ways: one detachment guarded the railway, one remained at Lutai, and he himself led the rest to defend Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 連奪陳家溝、跑馬廠、八里台，徑攻紫竹林，喋血八晝夜，敵來益眾，燃毒煙砲，我軍稍卻。

translations.literal: He successively took Chenjiagou, Paomachang, and Balitai, and pressed straight against Zilinzhu; for eight days and nights blood flowed, but the enemy came in still greater numbers, firing poison-smoke shells, and our troops gave ground slightly.
translations.idiomatic: He took Chenjiagou, Paomachang, and Balitai in succession and pressed straight on the Zilinzhu concessions; for eight days and nights the fighting was bloody, but the enemy came in ever greater numbers, fired poison-gas shells, and our troops were forced to give ground.

sentences.zh: 士成立橋上手刃退卒，顧諸將曰：「此吾致命之所也，逾此一步非夫矣！」

translations.literal: Shicheng stood on the bridge and himself cut down retreating soldiers; he turned to the generals and said: "This is where I give my life; one step beyond this is not the act of a man!"
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng stood on the bridge and himself killed fleeing soldiers; turning to his generals he said: "Here I lay down my life; any man who steps back from this spot is no man at all!"

sentences.zh: 遂殞於陣，腸胃洞流。

translations.literal: He then fell in battle, his entrails pouring from a gaping wound.
translations.idiomatic: He then fell in battle, his bowels torn open and spilling forth.

sentences.zh: 詔賜卹。

translations.literal: An edict granted posthumous benefits.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 閱二載，以世凱言，贈太子少保，諡忠節，建專祠。

translations.literal: Two years later, on Yuan Shikai's recommendation, he was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given the posthumous title Zhongjie, and a special temple was built.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, on Yuan Shikai's recommendation, he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given the posthumous name Zhongjie, and granted a special shrine.

sentences.zh: 羅榮光，湖南乾州人。

translations.literal: Luo Rongguang was a native of Qianzhou in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Rongguang came from Qianzhou in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 初隸曾國籓麾下，補把總。

translations.literal: At first he served under Zeng Guofan and was appointed platoon commander.
translations.idiomatic: He first served in Zeng Guofan's command and was appointed platoon commander.

sentences.zh: 同治初，李鴻章規三吳，從西將華爾克青浦，攻南橋鎮、柘林，直搗其巢，大敗之。

translations.literal: In the early Tongzhi period, when Li Hongzhang planned for the three Wu regions, he followed the Western officer Ward to Qingpu, attacked Nanqiao Town and Zhilin, drove straight at their nest, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi reign, as Li Hongzhang reorganized the lower Yangtze, he followed the Western officer Ward to Qingpu, attacked Nanqiao and Zhilin, struck straight at the rebel stronghold, and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 乘勝复沙川、金山，遷守備。

translations.literal: Following up the victory, he recovered Shachuan and Jinshan and was promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the advantage, he recovered Shachuan and Jinshan and was promoted to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 又從西將戈登釋常、昭圍，以次下太倉、崑山諸邑。

translations.literal: He also followed the Western officer Gordon in relieving Chang and Zhao under siege, and in succession took Taicang, Kunshan, and other districts.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Gordon in raising the sieges of Changzhou and Zhaowu, then took Taicang, Kunshan, and other towns in turn.

sentences.zh: 累擢參將。

translations.literal: He was promoted by stages to colonel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to colonel.

sentences.zh: 攻常州，先登，城复，遷副將，賜號果勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the attack on Changzhou he was first to scale the wall; when the city was recovered he was made deputy commander and granted the title Guoyong Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: At the assault on Changzhou he was first over the wall; when the city fell he was made deputy commander and granted the title Guoyong Batulu.

sentences.zh: 除狼山鎮右營游擊。

translations.literal: He was appointed mobile battalion commander of the right camp of Langshan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed mobile battalion commander of the right camp at Langshan.

sentences.zh: 蘇軍分援浙、皖、閩，連克湖州、長興、廣德、漳州、漳浦諸城，與有功，擢總兵。

translations.literal: When the Su Army was sent in relief to Zhejiang, Anhui, and Fujian, he helped take Huzhou, Changxing, Guangde, Zhangzhou, Zhangpu, and other cities, and for his merit was promoted to regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the Su forces were sent to aid Zhejiang, Anhui, and Fujian, he helped capture Huzhou, Changxing, Guangde, Zhangzhou, Zhangpu, and other cities, and was promoted to regional commander for his service.

sentences.zh: 六年，東捻擾魯疆，榮光以偏師游弋淮南北，敗捻於運。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the eastern Nian raided Shandong; Rongguang with a detached force ranged north and south of the Huai and defeated the Nian on the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: In 1867, when the eastern Nian raided Shandong, Rongguang led a detached column along the Huai and defeated them on the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 東捻回竄江、淮，分寇海、沭、邳、宿，並擊退之。

translations.literal: When the eastern Nian doubled back into the Jianghuai region and split to raid Hai, Shu, Pi, and Su, he beat them back on every front.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern Nian swung back into the Jianghuai and split to raid Hai, Shu, Pi, and Su, he drove them off on every front.

sentences.zh: 明年，西捻窺滑、濬，我師躡之，榮光戰數挫，而勇氣彌厲。

translations.literal: The next year the western Nian probed Hua and Jun; our forces pursued them; Rongguang was defeated several times, yet his courage grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the western Nian probed Hua and Jun; as our forces pursued them, Rongguang suffered several defeats, yet fought all the more fiercely.

sentences.zh: 鴻章謀困之黃、運間，緣河築長壘，榮光壁當敵衝，相持凡三閱月。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang planned to trap them between the Yellow and Grand Canals and built long ramparts along the river; Rongguang's wall faced the enemy's main thrust, and the standoff lasted three months.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang planned to trap them between the Yellow River and the Grand Canal and built long earthworks along the waterways; Rongguang's rampart lay in the enemy's path, and the standoff lasted three months.

sentences.zh: 會霖雨，寇多陷淖死，榮光復躡之東北，勢益蹙，張總愚自沉於河。

translations.literal: When heavy rains came many bandits sank in the mire and died; Rongguang pursued them northeast; their plight grew desperate, and Zhang Zongyu drowned himself in the river.
translations.idiomatic: When torrential rains came, many rebels sank in the mud and died; Rongguang pursued them northeast; their plight grew desperate, and Zhang Zongyu drowned himself in the river.

sentences.zh: 事寧，晉記名提督。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was advanced to brevet provincial commander.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was restored he was advanced to brevet provincial commander.

sentences.zh: 自是徙防金陵、武昌、西安，凡二年。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was transferred to garrison Jinling, Wuchang, and Xi'an over two years.
translations.idiomatic: He was then posted in turn to garrison Jinling, Wuchang, and Xi'an over two years.

sentences.zh: 移駐天津，補大沽協副將。

translations.literal: He moved to Tianjin and was appointed assistant regional commander of the Dagu garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Tianjin and appointed assistant regional commander of the Dagu garrison.

sentences.zh: 光緒七年，創設水雷營，遴各營將士演習，兼授化電測量諸學。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Guangxu he established a torpedo battalion, selected officers and men from every camp for drill, and also taught chemistry, electricity, and surveying.
translations.idiomatic: In 1881 he established a torpedo battalion, chose officers and men from every camp for training, and also taught chemistry, electricity, and surveying.

sentences.zh: 既而北塘、山海關相繼設，皆受成於榮光。

translations.literal: Soon Beitang and Shanhaiguan set up similar units in succession, all trained under Rongguang's direction.
translations.idiomatic: Beitang and Shanhaiguan soon followed with similar units, all trained under Rongguang's supervision.

sentences.zh: 醇親王閱北洋軍，以其教練有方，薦授天津鎮總兵。

translations.literal: When Prince Chun reviewed the Beiyang forces and found his training effective, he recommended him for appointment as regional commander of Tianjin garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Chun inspected the Beiyang army and found his training sound, he recommended him as regional commander of the Tianjin garrison.

sentences.zh: 位漸顯，服食儉約若老兵然。

translations.literal: As his position grew eminent, his dress and fare remained as spare as an old soldier's.
translations.idiomatic: Though his rank rose high, he dressed and ate as plainly as a veteran private.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，擢喀什噶爾提督，未之官而拳亂起，八國兵艦入寇，榮光守大沽砲台。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to provincial commander of Kashgar, but before he could take office the Boxer turmoil broke out; the armies of eight nations invaded by sea, and Rongguang defended the Dagu forts.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900 he was promoted to provincial commander of Kashgar, but before he could take office the Boxer uprising broke out; the fleets of eight powers invaded, and Rongguang held the Dagu forts.

sentences.zh: 大沽水深廣，河道縈曲，曲有台，備險奧，外兵懾其勢，弗敢進。

translations.literal: Dagu's waters are deep and broad, its channels winding; at each bend stands a fort, defensible and formidable, and the foreign armies feared its strength and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The waters at Dagu are deep and wide, the channels winding; forts stand at every bend, strong and hard to approach, and the foreign fleets feared them and held back.

sentences.zh: 榮光備益嚴，乃佯就款，使人言於裕祿，謂第得四五艘入口護僑商，無他意，裕祿許之。

translations.literal: Rongguang's defenses grew still stricter; the enemy then pretended to negotiate and sent word through Yulu that they sought only four or five ships to enter and protect their nationals, with no other intent—and Yulu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Rongguang tightened his defenses; the enemy then feigned negotiation and told Yulu through an envoy that only four or five ships wished to enter to protect their nationals, with no other intent—and Yulu consented.

sentences.zh: 榮光聞而大驚，力阻，而敵艦已踵入，將及台，遽出砲仰擊。

translations.literal: Rongguang was greatly alarmed on hearing this and strove to block them, but the enemy ships had already followed in; as they neared the forts he suddenly opened fire from above.
translations.idiomatic: Rongguang was appalled and tried to stop them, but the enemy ships had already entered; as they neared the forts he opened fire at once.

sentences.zh: 榮光再謁裕祿乞發戰令，諜者已報台毀，榮光憤極，歸，拔刀殺眷屬，曰：「毋令辱外人手！」

translations.literal: Rongguang again went to Yulu begging for the order to fight; spies had already reported the forts destroyed; in utmost fury he returned, drew his sword, and killed his dependents, saying: "Let them not fall into foreign hands!"
translations.idiomatic: Rongguang again begged Yulu for the order to fight; spies had already reported the forts lost; in fury he returned, drew his sword, and killed his family, crying: "They must not be shamed by foreigners!"

sentences.zh: 遂出赴難，一僕隨之，不知所終。

translations.literal: He then went out to meet death; one servant followed him, and neither was ever seen again.
translations.idiomatic: He then went out to die; one servant followed, and neither was ever seen again.

sentences.zh: 他日得其屍台下，僕屍亦在焉。

translations.literal: Days later his body was found below the fort, and the servant's corpse lay beside it.
translations.idiomatic: Days later his body was found below the fort, with the servant dead beside him.

sentences.zh: 沒三日而天津陷，時年六十有七。

translations.literal: Three days after his death Tianjin fell; he was sixty-seven years old.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjin fell three days after his death; he was sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 壽山，字眉峰，袁氏，漢軍正白旗人，黑龍江駐防，吉林將軍富明阿子。

translations.literal: Shoushan, styled Meifeng, of the Yuan clan, was a Bannerman of the Plain White, garrisoned in Heilongjiang, and son of Fuming'a, military governor of Jilin.
translations.idiomatic: Shoushan, styled Meifeng, of the Yuan clan, was a Plain White Bannerman garrisoned in Heilongjiang and son of Fuming'a, governor-general of Jilin.

sentences.zh: 以父任為員外郎，兼襲騎都尉世職，遷郎中。

translations.literal: Through his father's office he became an outer-court secretary, also inherited the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry, and was promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's position he became an outer-court secretary, also inherited the hereditary post of Commandant of Cavalry, and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十年，日軍犯奉天，自請赴前敵，充步隊統領。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Guangxu, when the Japanese invaded Fengtian, he volunteered for the front as commander of the infantry.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894, when the Japanese invaded Fengtian, he volunteered for the front as commander of the infantry.

sentences.zh: 弟永山領馬隊，數與日軍戰，复草河嶺，克連山關，進薄鳳凰城。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yongshan led the cavalry; they fought the Japanese repeatedly, recovered Caoling, took Lianshan Pass, and pressed close to Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yongshan led the cavalry; they fought the Japanese repeatedly, recovered Caoling, took Lianshan Pass, and pressed toward Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 敵援至，永山歿於陣，壽山被重創。

translations.literal: When enemy reinforcements arrived Yongshan died in battle and Shoushan was severely wounded.
translations.idiomatic: When enemy reinforcements arrived Yongshan fell in battle and Shoushan was badly wounded.

sentences.zh: 以敢戰，兼領鎮邊軍馬隊。

translations.literal: For his bold fighting he was also given command of the cavalry of the Frontier Defense Army.
translations.idiomatic: For his bold fighting he was also given command of the Frontier Defense Army's cavalry.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，降敕褒嘉。

translations.literal: A year later an imperial edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: A year later the throne issued an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 官軍既克海城，壽山領七十騎詣遼南诇敵勢，遇之湯岡子，搏戰，槍彈入右腹，貫左臀出，戰愈猛，敵稍卻，馳還壁，血縷縷滿衣袴。

translations.literal: After government troops recovered Haicheng, Shoushan led seventy horsemen to scout the enemy in southern Liaoning; at Tangangzi they met the enemy in battle; a bullet entered his right abdomen and passed out through his left hip; he fought all the fiercer; the enemy gave ground slightly; he galloped back to camp, blood streaming down his clothes.
translations.idiomatic: After the army recovered Haicheng, Shoushan led seventy horsemen to scout the enemy in southern Liaoning; at Tangangzi they fought; a bullet entered his right side and passed out his left hip; he fought all the harder; the enemy fell back slightly; he rode back to camp with blood soaking his clothes.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其勇，遷知府，賞花翎。

translations.literal: The throne praised his courage; he was promoted to prefect and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his courage; he was promoted to prefect and granted the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，調充鎮邊軍左路統領，徙駐黑龍江城。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was appointed commander of the left wing of the Frontier Defense Army and moved his headquarters to Heilongjiang City.
translations.idiomatic: In 1897 he was made commander of the left wing of the Frontier Defense Army and moved his headquarters to Heilongjiang City.

sentences.zh: 越二年，除知開封遺缺知府，未之官，值東北邊防亟，超改黑龍江副都統。

translations.literal: Two years later he was appointed to the vacant prefecture of Kaifeng but did not take office; with the northeastern frontier urgent, he was promoted out of turn to deputy lieutenant-general of Heilongjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was named to the vacant prefecture of Kaifeng but did not take office; with the northeastern frontier in crisis he was promoted out of turn to deputy lieutenant-general of Heilongjiang.

sentences.zh: 明年春，入覲，垂詢邊情甚悉，命佐將軍恩澤治軍。

translations.literal: The next spring he had an audience; the throne inquired minutely about border conditions and ordered him to assist General Enze in commanding the troops.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring he had an audience; the throne questioned him closely on border affairs and ordered him to assist General Enze in commanding the army.

sentences.zh: 疏請增募十五營，調諳邊事者十餘人，躬詣上海購軍械，自長崎、海參崴、伯利循海歸，潛度形勢，備戰守。

translations.literal: He memorialized to recruit fifteen additional battalions, summoned more than ten men versed in frontier affairs, went in person to Shanghai to buy arms, returned by sea via Nagasaki, Vladivostok, and Khabarovsk, secretly surveyed the terrain, and prepared for war and defense.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to recruit fifteen more battalions, called in more than ten men who knew the frontier, went himself to Shanghai to buy arms, returned by sea via Nagasaki, Vladivostok, and Khabarovsk, secretly surveyed the terrain, and prepared for defense.

sentences.zh: 新軍成，而恩澤卒於任，朝命代之。

translations.literal: When the new army was ready Enze died in office and the court ordered Shoushan to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When the new army was ready Enze died in office and the court ordered Shoushan to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 既蒞事，鏟姦弊，明賞罰，圖要塞；

translations.literal: Once in charge he rooted out corruption, made rewards and punishments clear, and planned strongpoints;
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he rooted out corruption, made rewards and punishments clear, and planned fortifications;

sentences.zh: 手訂行陣操法，頒之各將領，使番上，授以方略；

translations.literal: he personally drafted drill regulations for field formations and issued them to every commander, requiring them to take turns on duty and teaching them strategy;
translations.idiomatic: he personally drafted field-drill regulations and issued them to every commander, requiring rotation on duty and teaching strategy;

sentences.zh: 雖末弁亦接見，籍記備器使。

translations.literal: even junior officers he received and recorded what equipment each could supply.
translations.idiomatic: even junior officers he received in audience and recorded what equipment each could provide.

sentences.zh: 二十六年夏，拳亂作，俄軍數千聲為保護哈爾濱鐵軌，紛集海蘭泡，乞假道。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-sixth year the Boxer turmoil broke out; several thousand Russian troops, claiming to protect the Harbin railway, gathered at Hailanpao and asked passage.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of 1900 the Boxer uprising broke out; several thousand Russian troops, claiming to protect the Harbin railway, gathered at Blagoveshchensk and asked to pass through.

sentences.zh: 壽山曰：「敵偪我都，我假敵道，如大義何！」

translations.literal: Shoushan said: "The enemy presses on our capital; if we grant the enemy passage, what becomes of righteousness!"
translations.idiomatic: Shoushan said: "The enemy threatens our territory; if we let the enemy march through, what becomes of duty!"

sentences.zh: 拒之。

translations.literal: He refused.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 遂檄愛琿副都統鳳翔禦北路，呼倫貝爾副都統依興阿禦西路，通肯副都統慶祺禦東路，令各嚴戒備毋浪戰；

translations.literal: He then ordered Deputy Lieutenant-General Fengxiang of Aihui to guard the northern route, Deputy Lieutenant-General Yixing'a of Hulunbuir the western route, and Deputy Lieutenant-General Qingqi of Tongken the eastern route, instructing each to hold strict guard and not fight recklessly;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Deputy Lieutenant-General Fengxiang of Aihui to hold the northern route, Yixing'a of Hulunbuir the west, and Qingqi of Tongken the east, telling each to stand on guard and not fight recklessly;

sentences.zh: 並牒俄勿進兵，願負保路責。

translations.literal: and also notified the Russians not to advance, offering to bear full responsibility for protecting the railway.
translations.idiomatic: he also notified the Russians not to advance, offering to bear full responsibility for protecting the railway.

sentences.zh: 而俄軍已分道進，重以鐵路土工可十餘萬索值，倡罷工，揚言與俄為難。

translations.literal: But the Russian armies had already advanced on several roads; more than a hundred thousand railway laborers demanded back pay, called a strike, and openly threatened trouble with Russia.
translations.idiomatic: But Russian columns were already advancing on several roads; more than a hundred thousand railway laborers demanded wages, struck work, and openly threatened Russia.

sentences.zh: 壽山亟下令軍中曰：「保鐵路，護難民，全睦誼，違者殺無赦！」

translations.literal: Shoushan urgently ordered the army: "Protect the railway, shelter refugees, preserve friendly relations—whoever violates this shall be killed without mercy!"
translations.idiomatic: Shoushan urgently ordered the army: "Protect the railway, shelter refugees, preserve good relations—violators shall be executed without mercy!"

sentences.zh: 復使統領吉祥約富拉爾基監工蓋爾肖甫入城，俾釋疑懼，而蓋爾肖甫乃擊殺工人宵遁。

translations.literal: He also sent Commander Jixiang with Giershov at Fularji to supervise the work and enter the city to ease suspicion, but Giershov killed workers by night and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Commander Jixiang with Giershov at Fularji to supervise work and enter the city to ease fears, but Giershov killed workers by night and fled.

sentences.zh: 壽山猶強為容忍也，慎導俄民出境，籍錄其財物備還，然俄軍不為止，入寇愛琿及黑河屯，華人被迫赴水者，屍蔽江下。

translations.literal: Shoushan still forced himself to endure, carefully escorting Russian civilians out of the country and recording their property for return, yet the Russian army did not stop; it invaded Aihui and Heihe Tun; Chinese forced into the river left corpses covering the current downstream.
translations.idiomatic: Shoushan still forced forbearance, carefully escorting Russian civilians out and recording their goods for return, yet the Russians did not stop; they invaded Aihui and Heihe Tun; Chinese driven into the river left the water choked with corpses downstream.

sentences.zh: 三姓、呼倫貝爾又紛紛告警，壽山亟電吉林將軍長順會攻哈爾濱，然猶囑其語俄總監工，謂若罷兵，願以全家質。

translations.literal: Alarm came from Sanxing and Hulunbuir as well; Shoushan urgently wired the Jilin governor Chang Shun to join in attacking Harbin, yet still told the Russian chief engineer that if they halted he would stake his whole family as guarantee.
translations.idiomatic: Sanxing and Hulunbuir also sent alarms; Shoushan wired Jilin Governor Chang Shun to attack Harbin jointly, yet still told the Russian chief engineer that if they halted he would pledge his whole family.

sentences.zh: 當是時，諸路軍皆潰敗，北路統領崇玉，營官德春、瑞昌，西路統領保全，東路營官保林，並陷陣死，於是俄遂偪齊齊哈爾省城。

translations.literal: At that time every route's army was broken; on the northern route Commander Chongyu, camp officers Dechun and Ruichang, on the western route Commander Baoquan, on the eastern route camp officer Baolin—all fell in battle; the Russians then pressed on Qiqihar.
translations.idiomatic: By then every column had been broken; on the north Commander Chongyu and camp officers Dechun and Ruichang, on the west Commander Baoquan, on the east camp officer Baolin—all fell; the Russians then pressed on Qiqihar.

sentences.zh: 既而聞聯軍媾和，乃遣同知程德全往商和議，而自守「軍覆則死」之義，命妻及子婦先裁，手繕遺疏，猶惓惓於墾政，並致書俄將領囑勿戕民。

translations.literal: When word came that the allied powers had made peace, he sent Subprefect Cheng Dequan to negotiate, while he himself upheld the principle of "when the army is destroyed the commander must die"; he ordered his wife and daughters-in-law cut down first, wrote his final memorial still urging land reclamation, and wrote the Russian commanders asking them not to harm the people.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that the allied powers had made peace, he sent Subprefect Cheng Dequan to negotiate, while he upheld the rule of "a defeated commander must die"; he had his wife and daughters-in-law killed first, wrote his final memorial still urging land reclamation, and wrote the Russian commanders begging them not to harm civilians.

sentences.zh: 閱日，具衣冠，飲金，臥柩中，不死；

translations.literal: A day later, dressed in full regalia, he drank gold and lay in his coffin, but did not die;
translations.idiomatic: A day later, in full dress, he drank poison and lay in his coffin, but did not die;

sentences.zh: 呼其屬下材官擊以槍，不忍，手顫機動，彈出中左脅，猶不死；

translations.literal: he called his armorer to shoot him; the man could not bear to, his hand shook and the trigger slipped; the bullet struck his left ribs but he still did not die;
translations.idiomatic: he called his armorer to shoot him; the man could not bear to, his hand shook, the trigger slipped, the bullet struck his left side, yet he still lived;

sentences.zh: 更呼材官擊小腹，仍不死；

translations.literal: he called again for a shot in the lower abdomen; still he did not die;
translations.idiomatic: he called again for a shot in the lower belly; still he lived;

sentences.zh: 呼益厲，又擊之，氣始絕。

translations.literal: he shouted all the fiercer; they shot again, and only then did his breath stop.
translations.idiomatic: he shouted all the fiercer; they shot again, and only then did he die.

sentences.zh: 先是詔責其開邊釁，部議奪職。

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had blamed him for provoking border trouble and the Board voted to strip his office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier an edict had blamed him for provoking border trouble and the Board had voted to strip his rank.

sentences.zh: 後以總督徐世昌請復官，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，附祀富明阿祠。

translations.literal: Later, on Governor-General Xu Shichang's request, his office was restored; he was granted the hereditary offices of Commandant of Cavalry and Cloud Cavalry Captain, and given a place in sacrifice at Fuming'a's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at Governor-General Xu Shichang's request, his rank was restored; he was granted hereditary offices and given a place in sacrifice at Fuming'a's shrine.

sentences.zh: 族孫瑞昌，充北路營官，俄陷黑河，與統領崇玉同戰歿。

translations.literal: His clansman Ruichang served as northern-route camp officer; when the Russians took Heihe he fell in battle with Commander Chongyu.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Ruichang served as northern-route camp officer; when the Russians took Heihe he died fighting beside Commander Chongyu.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔，字集庭，漢軍鑲黃旗人，吉林駐防。

translations.literal: Fengxiang, styled Jiting, was a Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow, garrisoned in Jilin.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang, styled Jiting, was a Bordered Yellow Bannerman garrisoned in Jilin.

sentences.zh: 累官協領。

translations.literal: He rose by stages to assistant commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to assistant commandant.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十一年，中日事起，將軍長順赴奉督師，鳳翔任餽運，給食不乏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Guangxu, when trouble broke out between China and Japan, General Chang Shun went to Fengtian to command the army; Fengxiang handled transport and provisions never ran short.
translations.idiomatic: In 1895, when war broke out between China and Japan, General Chang Shun went to Fengtian to command; Fengxiang handled transport and food never ran short.

sentences.zh: 尋擢愛琿副都統。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to deputy lieutenant-general of Aihui.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to deputy lieutenant-general of Aihui.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，俄將固畢乃脫爾來假道，壽山令愛琿戒備。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Russian general Gubinadel came asking passage; Shoushan ordered Aihui to stand on guard.
translations.idiomatic: In 1900 the Russian general Gubinadel came asking passage; Shoushan ordered Aihui to stand on guard.

sentences.zh: 俄軍已自黑龍江下駛，翼日，俄官廓米薩爾名闊利士密德者，浮軍艦至，鳳翔遣軍拒之三道溝。

translations.literal: Russian troops had already sailed down the Amur; the next day the Russian officer Komissarov, called Kolishimide, arrived with gunboats; Fengxiang sent troops to resist him at Sandao Gou.
translations.idiomatic: Russian troops had already sailed down the Amur; the next day the Russian officer Komissarov arrived with gunboats; Fengxiang sent troops to meet him at Sandao Gou.

sentences.zh: 闊利士密德來謁，申前請，弗允，赬怒去，令舟師擊我，而我師已先發，殲其軍官二，闊利士密德被重創，奔還海蘭泡，旋卒。

translations.literal: Komissarov came to call and repeated the request; it was refused; he left flushed with anger and ordered his fleet to attack us, but our troops had already opened fire, killing two of their officers; Komissarov was badly wounded, fled back to Hailanpao, and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Komissarov came to call and repeated the request; it was refused; he left in anger and ordered his fleet to attack, but our troops had already fired, killing two officers; Komissarov was badly wounded, fled to Blagoveshchensk, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 於是黑河軍與海蘭泡俄軍相轟擊者數日。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Heihe army and the Russians at Hailanpao exchanged fire for several days.
translations.idiomatic: For days thereafter the Heihe army and the Russians at Blagoveshchensk exchanged fire.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔令統領王仲良率騎旅三百渡江擊之，始小挫，繼獲大勝。

translations.literal: Fengxiang ordered Commander Wang Zhongliang to lead three hundred cavalry across the river to attack; at first they met a small setback, then won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang ordered Commander Wang Zhongliang to lead three hundred cavalry across the river; at first they met a small setback, then a great victory.

sentences.zh: 俄軍緣江遁，師往馳之，會其軍艦泊江岸，載歸。

translations.literal: The Russian army fled along the river; our forces pursued; finding their gunboats moored on the bank, they towed them back.
translations.idiomatic: The Russians fled along the river; our forces pursued and towed back their gunboats moored on the bank.

sentences.zh: 閱二日，又渡江來，擊卻之。

translations.literal: Two days later they crossed the river again; we beat them back.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later they crossed again; we drove them back.

sentences.zh: 遲明，又率步旅六千自五道河濟，右路統領崇玉望見之，其軍皆樹我幟，衣我衣，意為漠河護礦兵也，弗敢擊，既登岸始覺，而勢已不可遏，我師敗績，崇玉殞於陣，愛琿陷。

translations.literal: At dawn they led six thousand infantry across from Wudao River; Commander Chongyu on the right wing saw them; their troops all flew our banners and wore our uniforms; he thought them the Mohe mineral-guard troops and dared not attack; only after they landed did he realize it, but the momentum could not be stopped; our army was defeated, Chongyu fell in battle, and Aihui was lost.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn six thousand infantry crossed from Wudao River; Commander Chongyu on the right saw them flying our banners in our uniforms and thought them the Mohe mineral guard; he dared not fire until they had landed; by then it was too late; our army was routed, Chongyu fell, and Aihui was lost.

sentences.zh: 壽山聞之，亟令鳳翔回援，弗及。

translations.literal: When Shoushan heard, he urgently ordered Fengxiang to return to aid him, but it was too late.
translations.idiomatic: When Shoushan heard, he urgently ordered Fengxiang back, but too late.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔駐兜溝子，去愛琿七十里。

translations.literal: Fengxiang encamped at Dougouzi, seventy li from Aihui.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang held Dougouzi, seventy li from Aihui.

sentences.zh: 踰月，俄軍復至，槍彈雨下，鳳翔以戰為守，相持累日。

translations.literal: A month later the Russians came again; bullets fell like rain; Fengxiang fought to hold his ground and the standoff lasted many days.
translations.idiomatic: A month later the Russians returned; bullets fell like rain; Fengxiang fought to hold and the standoff lasted many days.

sentences.zh: 黑龍江行軍故無棚帳，戰罷露宿，眾苦寒，以是軍有怨聲，鳳翔慮譁潰，復以地勢平衍難扼守，乃請壽山結陣徐退，抵內興安嶺軍焉，去兜溝子又百六十里。

translations.literal: Heilongjiang field armies had no tents; after battle they slept in the open; the men suffered bitter cold, and discontent arose; Fengxiang feared mutiny; the ground was also too flat to defend; he asked Shoushan to withdraw in good order to the Inner Xing'an Range army, another hundred sixty li beyond Dougouzi.
translations.idiomatic: The Heilongjiang troops had no tents and slept in the open after battle; the cold bred discontent; Fengxiang feared mutiny; the ground was too open to hold; he asked Shoushan to withdraw in order to the Inner Xing'an camp, another hundred sixty li beyond Dougouzi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，俄軍爭上嶺，勢洶洶，師失利，仍扼嶺拒之。

translations.literal: Before long the Russians pressed up the ridge in force; our troops met defeat but still held the pass against them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Russians pressed up the ridge in force; our troops were beaten but still held the pass.

sentences.zh: 敵攻益亟，鳳翔悉甲出，令曰：「有後者斬！」

translations.literal: As the enemy pressed harder Fengxiang sent out his entire force with the order: "Whoever falls back shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: As the attack intensified Fengxiang sent out his whole force with the order: "Whoever retreats shall be beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 而自赴前敵督懾。

translations.literal: He himself went to the front to oversee.
translations.idiomatic: He himself went to the front to command.

sentences.zh: 有材官稍卻，立使飛騎斬之。

translations.literal: When an armorer fell back slightly he immediately sent a flying courier to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: When an armorer gave ground slightly he sent a mounted courier to behead him at once.

sentences.zh: 材官懼，大呼陷陣，俄軍少卻，復進，遂大敗，署北路翼長恆玉斷一臂，俄將卒死傷無算。

translations.literal: The armorers in fear shouted and charged the line; the Russians fell back slightly, then advanced again, and were utterly defeated; Acting Northern Wing Commander Hengyu lost an arm, and countless Russian officers and men were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: The men in fear shouted and charged; the Russians fell back, advanced again, and were routed; Acting Northern Wing Commander Hengyu lost an arm, and countless Russians were killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔戰既酣，右臂左足兩受彈傷，墜馬者三，輒复躍上，鏖戰不少休，既還，嘔血數升而死。

translations.literal: Fengxiang fought with utmost fury; his right arm and left foot were both shot; three times he fell from his horse and leaped back up; he fought without pause; after returning he vomited several pints of blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang fought with all his might; his right arm and left foot were shot; three times he fell from his horse and leaped back up; he would not stop; after returning to camp he vomited blood and died.

sentences.zh: 事聞，優恤如製。

translations.literal: When word reached the throne, special posthumous benefits were granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, posthumous honors were granted by regulation.

sentences.zh: 崇玉，通肯正藍旗佐領。

translations.literal: Chongyu was an assistant commandant of the Plain Blue Banner at Tongken.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyu was an assistant commandant of the Plain Blue Banner at Tongken.

sentences.zh: 時同死事者，玉慶，黑龍江城世管佐領。

translations.literal: Those who died with him at the same time included Yuqing, hereditary assistant commandant of Heilongjiang City.
translations.idiomatic: Those who died with him included Yuqing, hereditary assistant commandant of Heilongjiang City.

sentences.zh: 城陷被執，詈不絕口，死最慘。

translations.literal: When the city fell he was captured; he cursed without cease and died most horribly.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he was taken alive; he cursed without cease and died most horribly.

sentences.zh: 扎魯布，黑龍江城水師四品官。

translations.literal: Zhalubu was a fourth-rank naval officer of Heilongjiang City.
translations.idiomatic: Zhalubu was a fourth-rank naval officer of Heilongjiang City.

sentences.zh: 懷印以殉，死後猶手握印不可脫。

translations.literal: He embraced his seal and died with it; after death his hand still gripped the seal and could not be opened.
translations.idiomatic: He died clutching his seal; after death his hand still held the seal and could not be pried open.

sentences.zh: 又段國英，宜黃人，以縣丞榷鹽阿什河。

translations.literal: Also Duan Guoying of Yihuang, who as assistant magistrate collected salt tax on the Ashi River.
translations.idiomatic: Also Duan Guoying of Yihuang, who as assistant magistrate collected salt tax on the Ashi River.

sentences.zh: 俄兵至，令讓所處屯兵，嚴詞拒之，縛而去；

translations.literal: When Russian troops arrived they ordered him to yield the garrison post; he refused in stern terms and was bound and taken away;
translations.idiomatic: When Russian troops came they ordered him to yield the garrison; he refused in the strongest terms and was bound and led away;

sentences.zh: 旋釋歸，則俄兵已佔其地，且懸俄幟，國英大哭曰：「中國亡矣！」

translations.literal: soon released, he found the Russians had occupied the place and raised their flag; Guoying wept aloud: "China is lost!"
translations.idiomatic: soon released, he found the Russians had occupied the place and raised their flag; Guoying wept aloud: "China is lost!"

sentences.zh: 觸石，頭裂，死。

translations.literal: He dashed his head against a rock and died.
translations.idiomatic: He dashed his head against a rock and died.

sentences.zh: 俄人觀者皆嘆息。

translations.literal: Russian onlookers all sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Russian onlookers all sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 論曰：秉衡清忠自矢，受命危難，大節凜然，此不能以成敗論也。

translations.literal: The commentators say: Bingheng kept his integrity and devoted himself to duty in peril; his great integrity was awe-inspiring—this cannot be judged by success or failure alone.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Bingheng held fast to integrity and took up duty in crisis; his great constancy commands respect—this cannot be judged by success or failure alone.

sentences.zh: 聯軍之佔津、海也，長驅而入，唯士成阻之；

translations.literal: When the allied armies occupied Tianjin and the coast they marched in at will; only Shicheng blocked them;
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies held Tianjin and the coast they advanced at will; only Shicheng stood in their way;

sentences.zh: 俄兵之侵龍江也，乘隙以進，唯壽山拒之：固知必不能敵，誓以一死報耳。

translations.literal: When Russian troops invaded the Amur region they advanced through every opening; only Shoushan resisted them: he knew full well he could not prevail, yet vowed to repay the state with his death.
translations.idiomatic: When the Russians invaded the Amur country they pressed through every gap; only Shoushan stood against them—knowing he could not win, yet sworn to repay his duty with his life.

sentences.zh: 榮光爭大沽，鳳翔守愛琿，雖已無救於大局，而至死不屈，外人亦為之奪氣，何其壯哉！

translations.literal: Rongguang fought for Dagu and Fengxiang held Aihui; though they could not save the larger situation, to the end they did not yield, and even foreigners were awed by them—how magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Rongguang fought at Dagu and Fengxiang held Aihui; though neither could alter the larger outcome, both died unbowed, and even the foreigners were struck with awe—how splendid their courage!
